name: Malabar Cancer Centre (Post Graduate Institute of Oncology Sciences & Research)
tagline: Regional government cancer institute serving North Kerala and neighbouring districts
summary: Government-run comprehensive oncology centre in Thalassery offering multidisciplinary cancer care, advanced radiotherapy, medical and surgical oncology, diagnostics and training.
description: Malabar Cancer Centre (MCC) is an autonomous institution under the Health & Family Welfare Department, Government of Kerala, set up to provide comprehensive oncology care for the northern region of Kerala and neighbouring districts. The centre (located at Moozhikkara, Thalassery) began as a regional cancer facility and has been developed into a postgraduate institute for oncology sciences and research. ([mcc.kerala.gov.in](https://www.mcc.kerala.gov.in/?utm_source=openai))

MCC offers multidisciplinary cancer services — radiation oncology, medical oncology, surgical oncology, clinical hematology, nuclear medicine, diagnostic radiology, laboratory and palliative care — with decisions taken in a multidisciplinary tumour board to plan individualised treatment. The institute also runs community oncology and a hospital-based cancer registry. ([mcc.kerala.gov.in](https://www.mcc.kerala.gov.in/treatment?utm_source=openai))

The centre is accredited (NABH) and its laboratories hold NABL accreditation; it has expanded clinical capabilities in recent years (including introduction of robotic surgery and advanced radiation planning systems) while developing Phase‑II and postgraduate training / fellowship programmes. These quality and capacity upgrades support complex care such as bone‑marrow transplant, pediatric haemato‑oncology and advanced imaging. ([mcc.kerala.gov.in](https://www.mcc.kerala.gov.in/storage/uploads/ckeditor_files/NABH%20renewal_1722406422.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Visitors (patients and caregivers) can expect an organised tertiary‑level cancer hospital with outpatient clinics, day‑care chemotherapy, inpatient wards, operating theatres, radiation therapy units and allied supportive services; for appointments, contact and directions use the official MCC site or contact pages and confirm timings before travel. ([mcc.kerala.gov.in](https://www.mcc.kerala.gov.in/location-map?utm_source=openai))
highlights: Autonomous regional cancer centre under Kerala Health & Family Welfare Department
Comprehensive multidisciplinary oncology: radiation, medical, surgical oncology and palliative care
Advanced services: PET/MRI/CT diagnostics, bone‑marrow transplant and robotic surgery
PG institute offering fellowships and an innovation/incubation initiative

sections.heading: Background
body: Malabar Cancer Centre was established to fill a regional gap in tertiary oncology services for North Kerala and neighbouring areas (including parts of Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and the Mahe enclave). The centre has been developed into the Malabar Cancer Centre — Post Graduate Institute of Oncology Sciences & Research (MCC‑PGIOSR) to combine patient care with training and research. ([mcc.kerala.gov.in](https://www.mcc.kerala.gov.in/storage/uploads/publications/169994422136.pdf?utm_source=openai))

sections.heading: Services & specialties
body: MCC runs clinical divisions in surgical oncology (including gynecological oncology), medical oncology, radiation oncology, clinical hematology, pediatric haemato‑oncology, nuclear medicine, radiology and allied support services such as physiotherapy, dietetics and psychology. The centre provides radiotherapy (dual‑energy linear accelerators, advanced planning systems), systemic chemotherapy, complex oncologic surgeries, bone‑marrow transplant programs and palliative care. Treatment plans are decided by a multidisciplinary tumour board. ([mcc.kerala.gov.in](https://mcc.kerala.gov.in/public/departments?utm_source=openai))

sections.heading: Facilities, research & training
body: MCC is NABH accredited and its labs hold NABL accreditation — markers of institutional quality and laboratory competence. The hospital reports upgraded IT and treatment‑planning systems (for example procurement of RayStation treatment planning for radiation oncology) and has introduced robotic surgery in recent years. The institute also runs fellowships and is developing incubation/support facilities for oncology innovation. ([mcc.kerala.gov.in](https://www.mcc.kerala.gov.in/storage/uploads/ckeditor_files/NABH%20renewal_1722406422.pdf?utm_source=openai))

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: MCC sits on a hilltop near Moozhikkara in Thalassery municipality (post: Moozhikkara, Thalassery 670103). Nearest rail: Thalassery Railway Station (~5 km); nearest bus stand: Thalassery bus stand (~4 km); nearest airport: Kannur International Airport (~26 km). Use the MCC contact page or official helplines to book appointments and confirm OPD days before travelling. ([mcc.kerala.gov.in](https://www.mcc.kerala.gov.in/location-map?utm_source=openai))

visitorInfo.bestTime: Year‑round; plan weekday OPD appointments in advance and confirm before travel.
visitorInfo.howToReach: Thalassery town — MCC is ~5 km from Thalassery Railway Station, ~4 km from the town bus station and about 26 km from Kannur International Airport; use local taxis or buses to Moozhikkara and follow MCC signboards. ([mcc.kerala.gov.in](https://www.mcc.kerala.gov.in/location-map?utm_source=openai))
etiquette: Book OPD appointments and confirm clinic days or procedures via the official MCC contact points before you travel.
Carry referral documents, previous reports and imaging on CD/USB where possible — multidisciplinary boards review prior records.
Ask about available government schemes, financial counselling and accommodation options in Thalassery; confirm costs and approvals directly with MCC.
If arriving by air, plan ground transfer from Kannur International Airport (approx. 26 km) and allow extra time for traffic.
